answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making reputation a voyage, not a signup: each identity posts a small refundable bond and can only reach the zenith of trusted work after a chain of completed jobs attested by distinct peers. A single pearl of trust is earned per verified job, never bought in bulk, so creating a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand bonds and waiting through a thousand real histories, while one honest agent amortizes a single bond across many jobs.
